title: The seg_contig cursor is advanced on a private copy and thrown away, so every epoch re-reads the identical head of every area and the exposure guard reports a number the run did not experience.
failure: DATA_SOURCE=real DATA_AREAS=eng DATA_CORPUS_CAP=200000 DATA_SEG_CONTIG=1 DATA_RESAMPLE=1 DATA_STREAM_BYTES=40000 RUN_EPOCHS=8. Measured: draw_stream(epoch=0/1/2) each return bytes exactly equal to bodies['eng'][:40000] (byte-identical, verified), and areas.cursors stays {'eng': 0} after every call. The run therefore sees 40,000 of the 190,000-byte body (21%) eight times and never sees the other 150,000 bytes, while data_plan's Gate data.exposure_max_planned prints 'armed, did not fire (1.6842 vs 2.0)'. Realized repetition on the material actually trained on is 8.0, i.e. 4x the guard's own threshold, and the guard exists precisely for P3-H22 ('py was memorised and eng was skimmed'). It also silently turns DATA_RESAMPLE=1 into the byte-identical-replay state the contract reserves for resample=False, with nothing reporting it.
evidence: Line 707 `cursors = dict(areas.cursors)` takes a COPY; line 729 `cursors[label] = start + want` writes only to the copy; the copy is never written back to `areas.cursors`, never returned on `Stream`, and `draw_stream` returns at line 751 discarding it. The docstring at lines 651-653 says the contiguous read comes "from a cursor that PERSISTS ACROSS EPOCHS, so an English-only run has only the text's own boundaries rather than discontinuities we manufacture every 8-20 KB", and `stream_state`'s docstring (lines 763-765) says "The cursors are LOAD-BEARING: without them a resume re-reads the head of every area under seg_contig and silently trains a second time on material the parent already used." The value it would checkpoint is permanently 0.
fix: Mutate `areas.cursors` in place (it is a plain dict on a frozen dataclass, which is why the field exists) rather than copying it -- `cursors = areas.cursors` -- or return the advanced cursors on `Stream` and have the composition root write them back. Store the cursor already reduced mod len(body) so the checkpointed value is bounded.
_triage_evidence: Same underlying code as the earlier cursor finding (src/data/api.py lines 716-799: cursors copied at 716, mutated at 775, never written back). Ran the exact scenario: DATA_SOURCE=real DATA_AREAS=eng DATA_CORPUS_CAP=200000 DATA_SEG_CONTIG=1 DATA_RESAMPLE=1 DATA_STREAM_BYTES=40000 RUN_EPOCHS=8. Measured epoch-0 and epoch-1 Stream.bytes were byte-identical in FULL (not just the first 40 bytes), and areas.cursors stayed {'eng': 0} after both calls -- confirming the run would see the same ~40,000-byte prefix on every epoch and never advance into the rest of the 190KB+ body, exactly the P3-H22-shaped failure round 1 describes. This is the most severe (round-1-rated 'critical') of the two cursor-copy titles and remains fully unfixed.

title: DATA_SEG_MIN=DATA_SEG_MAX=0 makes draw_stream loop forever
failure: With DATA_SEG_MIN=0 and DATA_SEG_MAX=0 (both zero-length), `want = stream.randint(seg_min, seg_max)` is always 0, so `chunk` is always b"", `len(out)` never advances, and the `while len(out) < hi:` loop at line 742 spins forever without ever hitting the phase bound. The run hangs with no error, no traceback, and no clock to time it out.
evidence: Reproduced live: `DATA_AREAS=eng DATA_SOURCE=real DATA_SEG_MIN=0 DATA_SEG_MAX=0` through open_areas -> data_plan -> draw_stream, run under `timeout 30`, process had to be killed (`Terminated`, exit 143) with no output after open_areas/data_plan succeeded. Traced by hand: `want=min(want, hi-len(out))=0`, `min(want, budget[idx])=0` (budget never depletes since chunks add 0 bytes), so `avail` never empties and the `if not avail:` rescue branch that would otherwise force progress is never reached. This is the still-live instance of round1's data/api.py:733 finding; the code is byte-for-byte unchanged since that finding was filed.
fix: Before the draw loop, refuse SEG_MIN==0 and SEG_MAX==0 (or more generally SEG_MAX==0) as a named startup condition (`DATA_SEG_MIN/SEG_MAX ... produces zero-length segments and would never terminate`), the same way SEG_MIN>SEG_MAX is refused; or clamp `want` to at least 1 byte per segment inside the loop and count it as a gate rather than looping silently.

title: the seg_contig cursor is copied into a local dict and thrown away, so it does not persist across epochs
failure: `cursors = dict(areas.cursors)` copies, `cursors[label] = start + want` mutates the copy, and nothing writes back to `areas.cursors`. Ran it at DATA_SEG_CONTIG=1, two synthetic areas, epochs=2: after `draw_stream(epoch=0)` `areas.cursors` is still `{'a': 0, 'b': 0}`, and epoch 1's first 40 bytes equal epoch 0's. Every epoch restarts each area from byte 0, so at RUN_EPOCHS>1 with resampling on the head of every corpus is trained on repeatedly and the tail is never reached -- and DATA.stream_state, documented to checkpoint "the per-area read cursors" because "without them a resume re-reads the head of every area under seg_contig", will checkpoint zeros.
evidence: Docstring: "True reads the body in order from a cursor that PERSISTS ACROSS EPOCHS". Body line 707 `cursors = dict(areas.cursors)`, line 729 `cursors[label] = start + want`, and the function returns at line 751 without ever assigning back into `areas.cursors`.
fix: Write the advanced cursors back into `areas.cursors` before returning (Areas is frozen but `cursors` is a mutable dict, which is why it is a dict), or return them on the Stream for the root to carry.
_triage_evidence: src/data/api.py line 716: `cursors = dict(areas.cursors)` copies; line 775 `cursors[label] = start + want` mutates only the copy; the function returns at line 799 without ever writing back into `areas.cursors`. Ran DATA_SOURCE=real DATA_AREAS=eng DATA_SEG_CONTIG=1 DATA_RESAMPLE=1 DATA_STREAM_BYTES=40000 RUN_EPOCHS=8: `areas.cursors` stayed `{'eng': 0}` after both an epoch-0 and an epoch-1 draw_stream call, and the two epochs' Stream.bytes were byte-identical in full (not just a 40-byte prefix). Confirms the cursor never persists.
_residue: None -- same defect as the 'critical' duplicate title below, unfixed on both.

title: DATA_DRAW=planned (the new shipped default) measurably worsens the pre-existing estimate-vs-realized gap in Gate data.splice_window, which H58's own rationale for defaulting to planned never accounts for
failure: Completely default configuration -- DATA_AREAS=eng,py,num,c, DATA_N_PROCESSES=4, DATA_SOURCE=synthetic, DATA_DRAW unset (so it resolves to the shipped default 'planned'), DATA_PHASES unset (shipped default 4), DATA_SEG_MIN/MAX unset (700/1800) -- with LM_CTX=128 and a measured TOK bytes_per_token near 1.213 (an ordinary value, not contrived beyond landing the ratio close to the gate's threshold): data_plan's Gate data.splice_window reports 'armed, did not fire (8.05 vs 8.0)' at every one of 8 tested seeds, i.e. it predicts the run is fine. The stream draw_stream actually produces has a realized mean-windows-per-segment of 7.43-7.97 in every one of those 8 seeds -- BELOW the 8.0 threshold every time -- so the gate is wrong in the same direction on 8/8 seeds at pure defaults. Re-running the identical scenario through the pre-H58 code (git show d8eadd5^:src/data/api.py, which is what DATA_DRAW=uniform now reproduces byte-for-byte) shows the SAME false-negative pattern already existed, but only on 6/8 seeds; DATA_DRAW=uniform on the new code also reproduces 6/8. So the gap is pre-existing (not created by H58) but the new default measurably worsens it (6/8 -> 8/8 flips at this config, and it grows with phase count: at DATA_PHASES=8/10/20/40 the average relative gap between the gate's predicted windows-per-segment and the realized value is 7.6%/10.4%/17.7%/32.3% under planned versus 3.7%/4.9%/10.0%/17.9% under uniform at the same phase counts -- roughly double, throughout). The owner's stated reason for defaulting to planned is 'a startup gate is the only thing that can refuse a bad configuration before it spends GPU time' (ISSUES P1-H58, DECISIONS D8); that reasoning is scoped to exposure_max/exposure_skew (the gates this commit did fix) and is silent about splice_window, a THIRD startup gate the same default now trusts less.
evidence: data_plan (api.py:641-646) computes `mean_seg = (int(dat.seg_min) + int(dat.seg_max)) / 2.0` and `windows_per_segment = mean_seg / (win_tokens * bytes_per_token)` BEFORE a single byte is drawn -- a static function of the declared seg_min/seg_max levers only. draw_stream's new 'planned' branch (api.py:739-766, added by d8eadd5) truncates every segment to `min(want, hi-len(out), budget[idx])`, so under the shipped default a segment is now cut short whenever an area's per-phase budget runs low, not only once at the very end of a phase (the old, sole 'uniform' truncation site, `want = min(want, hi-len(out))` alone). That is a strictly more frequent truncation trigger, so the realized mean segment length runs measurably below the seg_min/seg_max mean under planned more often than under uniform, and the gate's `reason` field (only populated for exposure_max/exposure_skew via the `caveat` variable at api.py:623-626) carries no caveat for splice_window even though it is the gate whose accuracy this same default choice is degrading.
fix: Either measure data.splice_window's windows-per-segment from the ACTUAL draw (move or duplicate the check into draw_stream once Stream.splice_starts exists, the same 'measured, not estimated' standard the docstring already claims for bytes_per_token at ISSUES P1-H16), or -- if it must stay a startup prediction -- compute mean_seg under 'planned' from the true per-phase-per-area budget distribution (min(seg_max, phase_span/live_count) truncation), and carry a `reason` caveat on this gate the same way exposure_max/exposure_skew already do, so a report can tell 'measured' from 'predicted, and predicted worse under this default' apart.

title: DATA_SEG_MIN > DATA_SEG_MAX passes every startup gate then dies inside the draw with an unnamed ValueError
failure: Nothing in open_areas or data_plan validates seg_min <= seg_max, so a DATA_SEG_MIN > DATA_SEG_MAX configuration builds a config and computes a Plan successfully. The crash only happens once draw_stream calls `stream.randint(seg_min, seg_max)`, and the resulting exception is CPython's own `ValueError: empty range for randrange()`, which names neither DATA_SEG_MIN nor DATA_SEG_MAX -- the exact 'refusal must name the lever' rule this codebase otherwise follows everywhere else in this file.
evidence:
Reproduced live: `DATA_AREAS=eng DATA_SOURCE=real DATA_SEG_MIN=2000 DATA_SEG_MAX=1000`. open_areas and data_plan both succeed and print gate values; draw_stream then raises:
```
ValueError: empty range for randrange() (2000, 1001, -999)
  File ".../data/api.py", line 758, in draw_stream
    want = stream.randint(seg_min, seg_max)
```
Still live -- identical to round1's data/api.py:717 finding; no commits have touched this file since that finding was filed (git log shows src/data/api.py unchanged since commit dd1ca9f).
fix: Add a startup refusal in open_areas or data_plan (or at the top of draw_stream, before any draw): `if int(dat.seg_min) > int(dat.seg_max): raise CorpusError(f"DATA_SEG_MIN={dat.seg_min} > DATA_SEG_MAX={dat.seg_max} ...")`, naming both numbers, so the refusal happens once at startup instead of nondeterministically inside the first draw of the first epoch.

title: draw_stream mints its per-epoch RNG stream with an unconditional again=True, disarming the duplicate-stream collision guard
failure: `_rng.rng_for(f"data.stream.e{int(epoch)}", seed, again=True)` passes again=True on every call with no rebuild (checkpoint restore or otherwise) to justify it. draw_stream's own docstring says it is 'Called once per epoch by the composition root, UNCONDITIONALLY', so under correct usage the guard would never trip anyway -- but with it permanently disabled, a caller bug that invokes draw_stream twice for the same epoch (a retry after a downstream exception, a duplicate call in a loop) silently gets two live generators replaying the identical sequence instead of the RngError this project relies on everywhere else to catch exactly this class of two-call-sites-one-sequence collision.
evidence: Reproduced live: called `draw_stream(dat, areas, plan, epoch=0, seed=1)` twice in one process (same areas/plan). No RngError raised on the second call; `st_a.bytes == st_b.bytes` is True -- the two 'independent' streams silently replayed the same values. With again=False (the normal rng_for behaviour used everywhere else, e.g. data.holdout.<key> and data.synth.<label>), the second call would instead raise `RngError: stream 'data.stream.e0' was already issued for seed 1`. This is the still-live instance of round1's data/api.py:702/707 finding (three other instances of this exact pattern -- lm.init, tok.dropout.mint, data.synth.<label> -- have already been repaired with the documented child-stream fix; this is the site that was missed).
fix: Drop `again=True` from the rng_for call at line 711 (nothing legitimately re-mints 'data.stream.e<n>' in one process), or if a genuine rebuild path exists, gate `again=True` on that specific condition and pass `again=False` on the ordinary call path so a genuine duplicate call is caught.

title: The seg_contig cursor is mutated on a local copy and never written back, so it does not persist across epochs as documented
failure: `cursors = dict(areas.cursors)` (line 716) makes a private copy; `cursors[label] = start + want` (line 775) updates only that copy. `areas` is a frozen dataclass and draw_stream never returns the advanced cursors anywhere the next call can read them, so every subsequent call to draw_stream re-reads `areas.cursors`, which is still all zeros from open_areas. Under DATA_SEG_CONTIG=True this means every epoch restarts reading each area from byte 0 instead of continuing where the previous epoch left off, directly contradicting the docstring's claim that the cursor 'PERSISTS ACROSS EPOCHS, so an English-only run has only the text's own boundaries rather than discontinuities we manufacture every 8-20 KB.'
evidence:
Reproduced live with DATA_RESAMPLE=1 (to force a fresh draw every epoch, ruling out the resample=False replay cache) and DATA_SEG_CONTIG=1, DATA_AREAS=eng, DATA_SOURCE=real:
  st0 = draw_stream(epoch=0), st1 = draw_stream(epoch=1)
  st0.bytes == body['eng'][0:len(st0.bytes)]  -> True
  st1.bytes == body['eng'][0:len(st1.bytes)]  -> True   (epoch 1 re-reads from byte 0)
  st1.bytes == body['eng'][len(st0.bytes):len(st0.bytes)+len(st1.bytes)] -> False  (the correct, cursor-persisted answer)
  areas.cursors after both epochs is still {'eng': 0}
Still live -- identical in mechanism to round1's data/api.py:707/733 findings ('the seg_contig cursor is copied into a local dict and thrown away'); unchanged since that finding was filed.
fix: Thread the advanced cursor dict back out of draw_stream (e.g. attach it to the returned Stream, or make Areas.cursors mutable state owned by a wrapper the composition root updates between calls) so the next epoch's draw_stream call starts from where the previous epoch left off, matching stream_state/restore_stream_state's stated job of checkpointing 'the per-area read cursors'.

title: On the default source=synthetic arm, DATA_AREAS is silently ignored and replaced with p0..pN-1 whenever it names fewer areas than DATA_N_PROCESSES
failure: `dat.source` defaults to "synthetic" (data/levers.py's `source = Lever("synthetic", ...)`), so an operator who sets only DATA_AREAS without also setting DATA_SOURCE=real gets the synthetic generator. `labels = entries[:n] if len(entries) >= n else [f"p{i}" for i in range(n)]` (line 373) means that whenever `len(entries) < dat.n_processes` (the default n_processes is 4), every declared area name is thrown away and replaced by generic p0..p3 labels -- the operator's DATA_AREAS value has no effect on the run at all, silently.
evidence: Reproduced live: `assemble.build(environ={"DATA_AREAS": "eng"})` (no DATA_SOURCE override) then `open_areas(...)`. Result: `areas.names == ('p0', 'p1', 'p2', 'p3')` -- the requested single area 'eng' never appears anywhere, and 4 synthetic Markov-process areas are trained on instead. No error, warning or refusal at any point; the config assembles and the pipeline runs to completion producing a result that has nothing to do with what was asked for. This is the still-live instance of round1's data/api.py:373 finding (label replacement) combined with the DEFAULT-SOURCE trap that makes it fire on the exact 'single area (DATA_AREAS=eng)' configuration this audit's Part 2 names.
fix: When `len(entries) < n`, refuse at startup naming DATA_AREAS and DATA_N_PROCESSES (e.g. 'DATA_AREAS names 1 area(s) but DATA_N_PROCESSES=4 synthetic processes were requested; name at least 4 areas or lower DATA_N_PROCESSES') instead of silently discarding the operator's area names. Separately, consider whether DATA_SOURCE defaulting to "synthetic" rather than "real" is the intended default given every real-data example in this audit and in data/ is reachable only by explicitly setting DATA_SOURCE=real.

title: The synthetic arm skips both declared collision refusals, so colliding area labels surface as a spine RngError naming neither the lever nor the paths
failure: DATA_SOURCE=synthetic with DATA_AREAS='rustA,rusta,x,y'. open_areas dispatches to _synthetic_areas at :221 BEFORE the label-collision and key-collision checks, which live only in the `else:` (real-corpus) branch at :239-259. _holdout_key('rustA') and _holdout_key('rusta') both give 'rusta', so :375 calls rng_for('data.synth.rusta', seed) twice. Reproduced: `RngError: stream 'data.synth.rusta' was already issued for seed 0. A second generator for one subsystem replays the same sequence...` -- an operator gets a message about generator identity for what the contract says is a startup refusal naming DATA_AREAS and both source paths.
evidence: Contract, open_areas docstring :117-123: 'two entries resolving to the same label are REFUSED with BOTH source paths printed (data.area_label_collision)'; and :140-146: 'TWO AREAS WHOSE KEYS COLLIDE ARE THE SAME STARTUP REFUSAL as the label collision above -- which is exactly the objection rng.py raises, answered at startup rather than papered over.' Body: `if str(dat.source) == "synthetic": raw, present, taken, sources = _synthetic_areas(dat, seed, entries)` at :220-221, with the two refusals unreachable from that path.
fix: Hoist the label and rng-key collision loop (:239-259) above the source branch at :220 so it runs on the entry list regardless of source, and let _synthetic_areas receive the already-validated (label, key) pairs.
_triage_evidence: src/data/api.py: open_areas dispatches to _synthetic_areas at line 220-221 (`if str(dat.source) == "synthetic": raw, present, taken, sources = _synthetic_areas(...)`) BEFORE the label/key collision loop, which lives only in the `else` branch at lines 240-258. Ran DATA_SOURCE=synthetic DATA_AREAS='rustA,rusta,x,y' through spine.assemble.build then data_api.open_areas: raised `RngError: stream 'data.synth.rusta' was already issued for seed 0. A second generator for one subsystem replays the same sequence...` -- exactly the round-1 reproduction, naming neither DATA_AREAS nor the colliding paths.
_residue: None -- the code path is unchanged from round 1's description.

title: Synthetic areas are labelled with the raw DATA_AREAS entry, slash included, while real areas are labelled with the basename -- one lever value, two label spaces
failure: DATA_AREAS='continual/01_rust,eng'. On the real arm open_areas:236 sets the label to `os.path.basename(entry.rstrip("/"))` = '01_rust'. On the synthetic arm _synthetic_areas:370 sets `labels = entries[:n]`, so the label is 'continual/01_rust'. Reproduced: `synthetic names: ('continual/01_rust', 'eng')`. Everything keyed by label then diverges between arms: per-area scores, Areas.rng_holdout keys, and DATA_PHASE_SCHED by name -- data_plan:523-529 looks each schedule token up in `by_name`, so PHASE_SCHED='01_rust|01_rust|01_rust|01_rust' (the documented pure-add spelling) resolves on the real arm and raises CorpusError('names '01_rust', which is neither an area index nor one of [...]') on the synthetic arm with the same DATA_AREAS.
evidence: :370 `labels = entries[:n] if len(entries) >= n else [f"p{i}" for i in range(n)]` versus open_areas :236 `labels.append((entry, os.path.basename(entry.rstrip("/")), os.path.join(str(dat.dir), rel)))`. The docstring rules the label at :112-114: 'the area LABEL is the basename ("continual/01_rust" labels as "01_rust")' -- stated without an exemption for the synthetic arm.
fix: Apply the same basename rule in _synthetic_areas: `labels = [os.path.basename(e.rstrip("/")) for e in entries[:n]] if len(entries) >= n else [f"p{i}" ...]`. Better, compute the (entry, label, key) triples once in open_areas before the source branch and pass them down.
_triage_evidence: src/data/api.py line 373: `labels = entries[:n] if len(entries) >= n else [f"p{i}" for i in range(n)]` uses the raw entry text, with no os.path.basename call, unlike the real arm's line 238 `os.path.basename(entry.rstrip("/"))`. Ran DATA_SOURCE=synthetic DATA_AREAS='continual/01_rust,eng' DATA_N_PROCESSES=2: areas.names == ('continual/01_rust', 'eng') -- the slash survives into the label on the synthetic arm, confirming the two-label-space divergence from the real arm.

title: open_areas and draw_stream produce none of the counters and gates their DID IT FIRE blocks declare, so DATA's armed-but-0 and unreachable states are indistinguishable everywhere
failure: On any run: Areas (returned at :313-315) carries names/bodies/holdout/holdout_bytes/bytes_present/bytes_taken/cursors/rng_holdout and no counters or gates field; Stream (returned at :729-737) carries no counters or gates field either. So data.corpus_cap_trip, data.val_cap_trip, data.area_open, data.area_nested, data.holdout_seam, data.holdout_overlap (all declared at :180-209) and data.stream_draw, data.segment, data.contig_wrap, data.resample, data.phase_entered (declared at :667-671) have no value anywhere in the returned records. Concretely: at DATA_SEG_CONTIG=0 the contract requires the report to say data.contig_wrap is UNREACHABLE with its arithmetic, and at DATA_SEG_CONTIG=1 to print how many wraps fired; the body has a bare comment `# data.contig_wrap` at :720 and no counter, so both read as nothing. data_plan is the only DATA entry point that returns Gate objects, which shows the mechanism was available and not used here.
evidence: open_areas DID IT FIRE, :180-209, names ten counters including 'data.corpus_cap_trip (fired N / armed but 0, prints taken vs present per area)' and 'data.holdout_seam ... Unreachable when a block lands at offset 0 or at the tail, which is the state it must say rather than read 0'. draw_stream DID IT FIRE, :667-671, names 'data.contig_wrap (unreachable at seg_contig=False, with the gate arithmetic)'. Neither Areas (:63-71) nor Stream (:410-...) has a counters or gates field, and spine/gate.py:24 Gate exists precisely so 'a reader can tell FIRED from ARMED-AND-INERT from UNREACHABLE across the entire report'.
fix: Add `counters: dict` and `gates: tuple` to Areas and Stream and fill them in both bodies -- taken vs present per area for corpus_cap_trip, the val_cap bite, one holdout_seam per area with Gate(reachable=False, reason=...) when the block lands at offset 0 or the tail, and a contig_wrap counter plus Gate(reachable=False, reason='DATA_SEG_CONTIG=0') on the other arm. data_plan's gates list (:604-623) is the pattern to copy.
_triage_evidence: Areas dataclass (line 52-71) fields: names, bodies, holdout, holdout_bytes, bytes_present, bytes_taken, cursors, rng_holdout -- no counters/gates field. Stream dataclass (line 412-428) fields: bytes, labels, splice_starts, area_changes, phase_bounds, area_names, per_area_drawn, epoch, stream_id -- also no counters/gates field. Verified programmatically: `hasattr(areas, 'counters')`, `hasattr(areas, 'gates')`, `hasattr(stream, 'counters')`, `hasattr(stream, 'gates')` all return False after a real open_areas/draw_stream call. data_plan is still the only DATA entry point returning Gate objects.

title: n_by_name is counted and then discarded, so the declared data.phase_name_resolved surface cannot exist
failure: `n_by_name` is initialised at line 528, incremented at 548 for each schedule entry given as an area name, and never read again -- Plan carries only (protocol, schedule, phase_bounds, per_area_draw, exposure, gates) and DATA has no counters() entry point, so nothing can report it. The contract makes 0 a positive statement ("every entry was an index, which is the shipped spelling and a statement rather than silence"), and that statement cannot be made either way. A run launched with the Q-DATA-7 name spelling ("rust|rust|rust|rust") and one launched with "1|1|1|1" produce identical artifacts.
evidence: Docstring: "DID IT FIRE: data.phase_resolved, data.protocol_named ..., data.phase_name_resolved (entries given as a NAME rather than an index; 0 means every entry was an index ...)". `grep -n n_by_name src/data/api.py` returns exactly lines 528 and 548.
fix: Carry the counter out -- either as a field the root reads off Plan, or as a Gate in Plan.gates (Plan already has a gates tuple), and do the same for data.phase_resolved / data.protocol_named.
_triage_evidence: src/data/api.py: `n_by_name = 0` at line 529, incremented at line 549 for each schedule entry resolved by name, and never read again anywhere in the file (grep for `n_by_name` returns only those two lines). Plan (line 396-409) carries only protocol/schedule/phase_bounds/per_area_draw/exposure/gates -- no field for it, and DATA has no counters() entry point (grep for 'def counters' in data/api.py returns nothing) to surface it another way.

title: draw_stream passes again=True on every epoch stream with no rebuild to justify it, disarming the duplicate-stream guard
failure: "data.stream" is not in compose.RNG_SUBSYSTEMS, so nothing pre-mints `data.stream.e0` and there is no collision to work around -- the flag is pure suppression. With it, a second `draw_stream(epoch=0, seed=S)` anywhere in a process (a re-draw after a restore, a harness that redraws an epoch, the isolation sweep) silently gets a second generator replaying the first one's sequence instead of the RngError that exists to catch it. This is the same flag whose use in tokenize produced P1-H56 ("three regularize=True calls on one text produced ONE distinct segmentation").
evidence: `stream = _rng.rng_for(f"data.stream.e{int(epoch)}", seed, again=True)`. rng.py: "again=True if you are deliberately rebuilding this stream (checkpoint restore)". The call-site comment justifies determinism across seeds and epochs -- which the NAME already buys -- not a rebuild. compose.RNG_SUBSYSTEMS = ("lm","sig","fabric","memory","domains","world","tok.dropout","data.synth","data.holdout","eval").
fix: Drop again=True. If a legitimate rebuild is needed (a resume that re-draws the epoch it was interrupted in), pass it only on that path and say so at that call site.
_triage_evidence: Same line as above, src/data/api.py:711, `again=True` unconditional on every call regardless of epoch or resume state. Demonstrated the guard is disarmed: called draw_stream(epoch=0, seed=0) twice in one process (no reset_issued, no restore/rebuild context) and the second call succeeded silently instead of raising RngError -- the exact 'two call sites, one sequence' collision spine/rng.py exists to catch.
_residue: None -- 'data.stream' is still absent from compose.RNG_SUBSYSTEMS (checked src/spine/compose.py:124-125), so there is still no pre-mint collision to justify the flag; the only concrete draw_stream call site in compose.py (line 1912-1913, epoch=0, in the assemble-time `compose()` function) calls it once, so the flag currently suppresses a collision that today's actual (non-stub) code never triggers -- but the flag itself, and the guard it disables, are unchanged from round 1.

title: On the REAL path a zero-size held-out block is recorded with the reason "source=synthetic holds nothing out", and nothing refuses the configuration that produced it.

title: `again=True` is passed unconditionally to rng_for with no justification, disabling the one guard against two call sites sharing a stream name.
failure: The composition root's own tables call draw_stream twice for epoch 0 -- ASSEMBLY_ORDER's `stream` row (compose.py:1902, epoch=0) and LOOP_ORDER's `E` row (compose.py:687, epoch=clock.epoch, which is 0 on the first epoch). Two generators are therefore issued for `data.stream.e0` in one run, and `again=True` makes that silent. Any further consumer that asks for `data.stream.e<n>` -- a diagnostic, an eval replay, a future stratified draw -- receives a generator replaying DATA's exact sequence while believing it has its own, and neither RngError nor rng.issued() (which records one entry per name) can show it.
evidence: Line 702 `stream = _rng.rng_for(f"data.stream.e{int(epoch)}", seed, again=True)`; the comment above it (lines 698-701) explains the epoch-keyed NAME and says nothing about `again`. spine/rng.py's Rng.__init__ documents the flag as "a legitimate rebuild of one stream (checkpoint restore) passes again=True and says so at the call site", and the module header calls two call sites on one name "the thing this whole module removes".
fix: Drop `again=True`; if the root genuinely draws epoch 0 twice, have the second caller reuse the Stream (as the resample=False path already does) or call reset_issued() between runs. If a checkpoint-restore rebuild really needs it, pass it only on that path and say so in the comment.
_triage_evidence: The core defect (line 711, `again=True` unconditional, no rebuild context, guard disarmed) is unchanged and verified live: a second draw_stream(epoch=0, seed=0) call in one process succeeds silently instead of raising RngError. However, the SPECIFIC failure narrative round 1 gave for this title -- 'the composition root's own tables call draw_stream twice for epoch 0 -- ASSEMBLY_ORDER's stream row (compose.py:1902) and LOOP_ORDER's E row (compose.py:687, epoch=clock.epoch, which is 0 on the first epoch)' -- no longer holds against the current compose.py: there is exactly ONE actual call site to data_api.draw_stream in executable code (compose.py line 1912-1913, epoch=0, inside the real compose() function). LOOP_ORDER is a documentation-only tuple (explicitly commented 'NOT EXECUTED HERE -- the loop is RUN mechanism'), and its own comment at compose.py lines 651-664 now states the E-stage's epoch-0 rows come ONLY from ASSEMBLY_ORDER and that 'THE E ROWS IN THIS TABLE NEVER RUN ON A ONE-EPOCH RUN' -- LOOP_ORDER's E row only re-enters on Tick.rolled, i.e. after epoch has already incremented past 0, so it would pass epoch>=1, not epoch=0. The loop driver itself (RunClock.advance/begin_epoch in train/api.py) is still an unwritten stub, so the double-epoch-0-call scenario cannot even be exercised today. So: the underlying vulnerability (unjustified again=True disabling the guard) is confirmed still live, but the specific 'two generators for data.stream.e0 in one run' reproduction this title's failure text relies on is not reproducible against the current tree's documented composition order.
_residue: The again=True flag itself remains unjustified and unfixed (verified live), but the concrete epoch-0 double-call path this title's evidence cites is no longer accurate as compose.py is currently written/commented -- treat the general guard-disarming as still-present and the specific ASSEMBLY_ORDER/LOOP_ORDER double-call story as unverifiable/likely stale.

title: The 'planned' law's per-phase budget dict uses assignment, not accumulation, so it silently disagrees with data_plan's per_area_draw (which DOES accumulate) the moment a phase's live-area list repeats an index -- and the code's own comment claims the two 'agree by construction', which is false

evidence: api.py:739-741 builds the phase's budget with `budget = {}` then `for j, idx in enumerate(live): budget[idx] = span // len(live) + (1 if j < span % len(live) else 0)` -- an ASSIGNMENT keyed by idx, so a repeated idx within `live` silently overwrites rather than sums its shares (data_plan's own per_area_draw at api.py:591-598 uses `per_area_draw[names[idx]] += share`, the accumulating form, on the identical per-j formula). The comment at api.py:735-737 states 'Both use the same rule -- floor division with the remainder on the first live areas -- so the two agree by construction and not by coincidence'; they in fact agree only because data_plan's schedule parser happens to dedupe every phase via `tuple(dict.fromkeys(live))` (api.py:565) and derive.phase_schedule's generated phases are always a contiguous `range()` with no repeats (spine/derive.py:727) -- an invariant enforced entirely OUTSIDE this function, which draw_stream neither checks nor is told about. Confirmed unreachable through the real composition-root path today: spine/compose.py:1911-1912 always feeds draw_stream the very Plan data_plan just produced, and a 180-trial randomized sweep across area counts/phase counts/stream_bytes/seg sizes/phase_live/seg_contig through the real entry points never produced a duplicate index or a nonzero deviation.

title: the resample=False replay cache is keyed by id(areas), an address CPython reuses, so the stated per-Areas isolation does not hold and every Stream is retained forever
failure: `id()` is only unique among live objects. Demonstrated: after freeing one Areas, a newly built Areas landed on the same address within 134 allocations in the same interpreter -- exactly the isolation-sweep scenario the comment names. A stale entry from a freed run is then returned to a different run for any epoch>0 request that precedes that run's own epoch-0 draw. Independently, `_REPLAY` holds every Stream (bytes plus a per-byte labels list) for the life of the process with no eviction, so a sweep of many runs per interpreter leaks one full stream per run.
evidence: Comment above `_REPLAY`: "Keyed by the Areas object rather than by a module global holding one stream, so two Areas in one process (the isolation sweep runs many 200-step runs per interpreter) cannot hand each other's text back." Body: `_REPLAY[id(areas)] = st` and `cached = _REPLAY.get(id(areas))`.
fix: Cache on the Areas object itself (a mutable field the record already permits, like `cursors`) or use a `weakref.WeakKeyDictionary`, so the entry dies with the Areas rather than outliving its address.
_triage_evidence: src/data/api.py: `_REPLAY = {}` module-level dict (line 805); `cached = _REPLAY.get(id(areas))` (line 702) and `_REPLAY[id(areas)] = st` (line 798) are unchanged -- keyed by the CPython object address, no weakref, no eviction. CPython does reuse addresses of freed objects (demonstrated with a small repro: freeing and reallocating small objects reused an id within 2 allocations), so the described isolation-sweep collision remains structurally possible, and the dict still has no eviction path, so every resample=False Stream is retained for the life of the process.

title: `seam_at` is recorded as the block offset unconditionally, so a block at offset 0 or at the tail reports a manufactured seam that does not exist -- the unreachable state the contract requires it to say.
failure: When the drawn `start` is 0 the removal takes a prefix and leaves no manufactured discontinuity, yet the record reads seam_at: 0, which a report renders as a seam at position 0. When start + n_hold == len(blob) the removal takes the tail and again leaves no seam, yet the record reads seam_at: start -- an offset that is the END of the body. Either way the data.holdout_seam reading counts a discontinuity the body does not contain, and DATALevers' claim that the only boundaries left under seg_contig are the text's own is checked against a number that is wrong in exactly the two cases where the claim is true.
evidence: Line 305 `rng_holdout[label] = {..., "seam_at": start}` with no test on start or start + n_hold. The DID IT FIRE list at lines 189-194 requires the opposite: data.holdout_seam is "Unreachable when a block lands at offset 0 or at the tail, which is the state it must say rather than read 0".
fix: Set `"seam_at": start if 0 < start and start + n_hold < len(blob) else None`, with a `why` naming which of the two boundary cases applies, so the report can print UNREACHABLE rather than a position.
_triage_evidence: src/data/api.py lines 304-305: `rng_holdout[label] = {..., "seam_at": start}` with no test on `start` or `start + n_hold`. Forced start=0 by monkeypatching `Rng.randint` to always return 0 (class-level patch, since Rng uses __slots__) and ran open_areas on DATA_AREAS=eng DATA_HOLDOUT_FRAC=0.3: got `rng_holdout['eng'] == {'key': 'data.holdout.eng', 'offset': 0, 'size': 6000, 'seam_at': 0}` -- seam_at reads 0 (a position) instead of None/UNREACHABLE at exactly the boundary case the docstring says must be UNREACHABLE.

title: data.holdout_overlap is never computed, so the one instrument declared for near-duplicate contamination between the held-out block and the training body produces no number at all.
failure: The contract makes the overlap a per-area reading printed once at startup and states why the split rule alone cannot answer it (Lee et al. arXiv:2107.06499: models "underestimate perplexity on evaluation documents with near duplicates", so "NEITHER the tail nor the random block is safe on its own"). open_areas computes nothing of the kind and `Areas` carries no field for it -- `rng_holdout` holds key/offset/size/seam_at only. A run on data/train/eng, whose seven files include dracula.txt while data/continual/03_dracula exists as a separate area, has no way to report that its held-out English overlaps its training material, and every held-out b/B figure the project publishes is uncontrolled for it.
evidence: Lines 211-316 contain no n-gram or overlap computation; the returned Areas fields are fixed at lines 64-71. The DID IT FIRE list at lines 195-202 declares data.holdout_overlap as "a READING, not a lever and not a gate: the fraction of held-out bytes that also occur verbatim in the training body at a fixed n-gram length, per area, printed once at startup. It costs no lever, no wire and no default, and it answers the one question the split rule CANNOT".
fix: Compute the fraction of held-out bytes covered by n-grams (fixed length, e.g. 50) that also occur in bodies[label], and carry it per area on rng_holdout so the startup banner can print it beside the offset and size.
_triage_evidence: grep for 'overlap' in src/data/api.py matches only the docstring prose at line 195 declaring the DID-IT-FIRE surface; there is no n-gram/overlap computation anywhere in the file, and Areas.rng_holdout entries (verified via the live open_areas runs above) contain only key/offset/size/seam_at(/why) -- no overlap fraction field exists on Areas or anywhere else in the returned records.

title: seam_at is recorded as the block's offset unconditionally, so a held-out block landing at byte 0 or at the tail reports a manufactured seam that isn't there
failure: `rng_holdout[label] = {..., "seam_at": start}` (line 305) always records `start` as the seam position with no check for whether `start == 0` or `start + n_hold == len(blob)`. The docstring's own DID IT FIRE contract for data.holdout_seam says this is 'Unreachable when a block lands at offset 0 or at the tail, which is the state it must say rather than read 0' -- but the code has no branch that ever produces that unreachable state; every held-out block, regardless of where it lands, is reported as manufacturing exactly one interior seam.
evidence: Static: lines 287-305 contain no conditional on `start` or `start + n_hold` before setting seam_at; the field is set unconditionally on every path through the `n_hold > 0` branch. Confirmed the randint draw is inclusive of both endpoints (`stream.randint(0, len(blob) - n_hold)`), so offset 0 and the tail are both reachable outcomes of ordinary operation, not edge cases requiring adversarial input. Still live -- identical to round1's data/api.py:305 finding; the file is byte-for-byte unchanged in this region since that finding was filed.
fix: After computing `start`, set `seam_at = start if 0 < start and start + n_hold < len(blob) else None` (or a similar boundary check) so the docstring's declared unreachable state is actually reachable and printed rather than silently never occurring.

title: data.holdout_overlap is declared as a startup reading but never computed anywhere
failure: The docstring declares `data.holdout_overlap` as 'a READING, not a lever and not a gate: the fraction of held-out bytes that also occur verbatim in the training body at a fixed n-gram length, per area, printed once at startup' -- the one instrument this package has for near-duplicate contamination between the held-out block and the training body. No code anywhere in open_areas (or anywhere else in this file) computes an n-gram overlap between `holdout[label]` and `bodies[label]`.
evidence: `grep -n holdout_overlap src/data/api.py` returns exactly one hit, the docstring line itself (195); no assignment, no function, no return value carries this reading anywhere in the module. Still live -- identical to round1's data/api.py:211 finding.
fix: Compute the declared n-gram overlap between `holdout[label]` and `bodies[label]` for each area after the split and surface it (e.g. as a field on Areas, or through the same reporting channel the other DID IT FIRE rows use), or narrow the docstring if this reading is being deferred to a later package version.

title: n_by_name is counted while parsing DATA_PHASE_SCHED but discarded -- data.phase_name_resolved cannot exist
failure: `n_by_name` is incremented every time a DATA_PHASE_SCHED entry resolves as an area NAME rather than an index (line 549), but it is never placed on `Plan` (whose fields are protocol, schedule, phase_bounds, per_area_draw, exposure, gates) or returned any other way. The docstring's declared DID IT FIRE row `data.phase_name_resolved` therefore has no value to report; the count is computed and then thrown away.
evidence: `grep -n n_by_name src/data/api.py` shows only the initialisation (line 529) and the increment (line 549); `Plan`'s field list (lines 396-409) has no matching field, and the `return Plan(...)` statement (line 648) does not mention it. Still live -- identical to round1's data/api.py:548 finding.
fix: Either add a `phase_name_resolved` field to Plan and populate it with `n_by_name`, or surface it through whatever counters mechanism is added for the open_areas/draw_stream gap above.
